prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: for each month of 2025, how many users were invited to LedgerLoop accounts? invited_at holds Brussels time: take the month as stored. Every month of 2025 has a row, and a month with no invited users shows 0. Return two columns, in this order: month (the first day of the month) and users_invited. Return one row for each month. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, look at the join between the months and the counts: which months can it lose?
An inner join keeps only months that have a count, so a month nobody was invited in disappears before COALESCE can turn it into 0.
starter_sql:
WITH months AS (
  -- one row per month of 2025
  SELECT CAST(range AS DATE) AS month
  FROM range(DATE '2025-01-01', DATE '2026-01-01', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
), invited AS (
  -- one row per month with invited users
  SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', invited_at) AS DATE) AS month, COUNT(*) AS users_invited
  FROM users
  WHERE invited_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND invited_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY CAST(date_trunc('month', invited_at) AS DATE)
)
SELECT m.month, COALESCE(i.users_invited, 0) AS users_invited
FROM months m
JOIN invited i ON i.month = m.month
why_this_works: With LEFT JOIN every month of the spine stays, so a month with no invited users reaches COALESCE and shows 0.
